outcome.technical: REPRODUCED on the real commands (probe: SG2.15's, copied and extended, on a copy of HEAD's plugin, repro.out): (a) a wave whose SECOND member's pin changed - subagent route: the stopped step leaves dispatched-executor[P1.1] in the drive's state, the next `next` after restoring the bytes prints only P1.2, and a `next` after that says `decide no-executor-return P1.1`; session route: dispatched-executor and writer[P1.1] left behind, then `wait P1.1: the writer session has written no record`; (b) a resume: after the stopped `--answer resume` the pending decision is gone and the same answer is refused (`no decision is pending for P1, so --answer resume answers nothing`, exit 2), a resume prompt file left on disk. NOT reproduced as a failure of its own: (c) the window between the pre-check and the command's building cannot be hit deterministically by real commands (a file would have to change between two reads inside one process); it is shown by spd18 and spd18b, which change the bytes in between and are red on HEAD (PinStop after the mark, no dispatch recorded). Also seen on HEAD: a wave whose FIRST member's pin changed leaves the wave recorded, both members started and a tree cut before the stop (no dispatch mark, so benign in effect, but not a state equal to before). FIXED in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py: (1) ask_member_pins reads the pin of every member that owes its executor (owes_executor: the _writer_turn facts, no action) before the wave is recorded (wave_step) and before any member is stepped (walk_wave), naming the member; (2) walk_wave's second shape: a member that stops (returned stop or raised ValueError) after an earlier member was handed out leaves that member printed, the stop a warning on the print, ctx stop kind cleared; (3) dispatch asks its tree, writer setting, pins (session_hand: ONE read, names and --skill-pin flags) and the review-fix reading before its brief and its mark; writer_argv builds the command from that read (held), also for reviewer_dispatch and review_fix_dispatch; (4) apply_answer sends a resume to resume_writer(consume=True) before consuming anything, and resume_writer drops the pending decision and spends the gated mark only after the tree, the writer setting, the pins and the prompt, the dispatch's own write recording both. --answer redispatch is deliberately NOT moved (what it did stays recorded and the reviewer is the drive's own next move; spd16 holds that). Docs: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (a paragraph in the drive-phase.py section; the run-agent-session.py paragraph on dispatch and writer_argv), CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry under Unreleased (heading untouched). TESTS (tests/test_drive_phase.py, block spn-block, one new function _pin_stop_state_cases and helpers after _pin_load_cases): spd10 one task each route, whole kept state equal; spd11/spd12 wave second/first member, kept state equal, plan untouched, member and skill named, nothing started, on both routes; spd13 restore then the same command hands both members out, print equal line for line to the same wave with no pins; spd14/spd15/spd15a resume stop keeps the decision, gated mark and every file under the state directory, the same answer then resumes with the pin on the command, a no-pin plan resumes as before; spd16 redispatch; spd17/spd17a which members are asked, a plan with no pins asks and reads nothing; spd21 an open wave asks before stepping; spd18/spd18b the command is built from the pre-check's read (executor and reviewer sessions); spd19 the review-fix reading is asked before the mark; spd20 the second shape. spd9 was changed (a plan with a pin now loads the manifest as often as one without, 1 time: the pre-check's read is the one the command is built from). REPOSITORIES BUILT per new case: spd10 two (one per route, copies of cached templates the existing spd cases already build, one git add and one commit each); spd11-spd13 together four wave repositories (two per route: the pinned wave, whose one repository serves all three cases through two stopped steps and one dispatching step, and a plan-with-no-pins twin for the line-for-line comparison), each _wave_repo copy plus about four git calls, four more commits in the pinned one, and one new template (two tasks) built once per run; spd14-spd21 none (a temp directory, no git). The whole-suite sweep ran twice (6:33 with the first defect, 5:57 after, --jobs 4); the block alone runs 10-35 s here, across the 22 mutation rows. NOT RUN: windows.
